title: Home Mortgage Loans: Delinquency Status and Return to Active
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Delinquency Status and Return to Active

The status of a loan under Home Mortgage Loans changes to delinquent when an installment stays unpaid too long, and changes back once the arrears are cleared. This page states both movements and the matters that sit outside servicing policy.

## Clauses

**Becoming delinquent.** A loan becomes delinquent when an installment remains unpaid 30 days after its due date. The days past due are read from the bank's loan records.

**Returning to active.** A delinquent loan becomes active again once every past-due installment has been paid, together with the escrow owed with them. When that happens, the loan's days past due go back to zero.

**Matters outside this policy.** Decisions on foreclosure, short sale and deed-in-lieu are not made under this policy.

## Status movements at a glance

| Starting status | Event | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|
| active | an installment unpaid 30 days past its due date | delinquent |
| delinquent | all past-due installments and escrow paid | active |
| delinquent | payment in full of the loan | paid off |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical loans)

- A loan whose oldest unpaid installment shows 30 days past due in the bank's records has reached the mark, and the loan becomes delinquent.
- A loan whose unpaid installment shows 29 days past due has not reached the mark and remains active.
- A delinquent loan has two past-due installments and the borrower pays only the older one. One past-due installment remains, so the loan stays delinquent; once the second is paid as well, it returns to active.

These loans and installments are invented for illustration.
